# m0serve

> Realtime from a synchronous Python app, with no added infrastructure.
> A WSGI/ASGI server written in Mojo: `pip install m0serve` — no Mojo
> toolchain, no dependencies, nothing fetched at install. Its distinguishing
> capability: held SSE and WebSocket connections gated by plain synchronous
> views (Django, Flask, ...), with cross-worker publish — no Channels, no
> Redis, no daphne, no second process. It is NOT the fastest server on raw
> throughput and docs/BENCHMARKS.md says so with numbers.

Platforms: macOS arm64 (13+), Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (glibc; the exact
floor is in the wheel filename — pip refuses rather than crashes on older
systems). CPython 3.10–3.14, free-threaded builds included; one wheel per
platform because the binary dlopens libpython rather than linking it.
No Windows, no musl, no TLS/HTTP2 (terminate at a proxy).

## Operating contract

- `m0serve MODULE[:ATTR]` serves WSGI or ASGI, detected from the object.
  Bare `MODULE` tries `MODULE.asgi:application`, `MODULE.wsgi:application`,
  `MODULE:app`, `MODULE.main:app`.
- Flags are strict and named in `m0serve --help`; flags override `M0_*`
  environment variables, which override defaults.
- Refusals explain themselves on stderr and name the fix; a configuration
  the server will not run exits 78. `--version` prints `m0serve X.Y.Z`.
- `m0serve --doctor [OPTIONS] [MODULE]` prints one JSON object and starts
  nothing — platform and wheel arch, the interpreter it resolved and where
  it lives, the application spec discovery chose and the protocol it
  classified as, the resolved topology (including whether the handler pool
  is a default or configured), and a `checks` array in which every failure
  carries `detail`, `fix` and `exit`. **It exits with the code `m0serve`
  itself would exit with for the same arguments** (0 serve, 2 usage,
  1 startup, 78 EX_CONFIG), so it answers "will this run?" without binding
  a port, forking, or importing the app twice. `poe smoke-doctor` runs both
  over every refusal and compares. Bare `--doctor` with no MODULE is the
  environment check and exits 0.
- `--health-path /health` answers 200 in the server, before Python.
- Realtime: a view's response with `M0-Hold: stream|websocket` +
  `M0-Channel: NAME` converts the connection to a held subscription;
  `from m0serve import m0pub; m0pub.publish(channel, data)` reaches every
  subscriber on every worker. Inbound WebSocket messages arrive as POSTs
  to `/ws/message` with `M0-Channel`/`M0-Slot`/opcode headers. `--realtime`
  composes with `--blocking-threads` and `--mount`, so held connections,
  an ASGI mount and a handler pool can share one process; it is refused
  only where nothing could take a hold (an ASGI-only server).

## Start here

- [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md): ten minutes to live multi-tab sync from
  one sync-Django file. Every fenced block is executed by CI on every pull
  request (`poe smoke-quickstart`), so the steps are pinned, not aspirational.
- [README.md](README.md): install matrix, framework docs, limits.
- [docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md): the capability matrix — what this
  server implements and what proves it, one row per capability with a
  named CI gate, a source file, a roadmap heading or a reason for the
  refusal. `docs/spec.json` is the same data, generated from it.
  `verified` there means a gate runs on the stated cadence, not that
  the capability is correct; the page says so itself.
- [docs/BENCHMARKS.md](docs/BENCHMARKS.md): every performance number, each
  rendered from a dated artifact in `bench/results/` and CI-checked against
  it. States where m0serve loses (raw throughput, against both Granian and
  uvicorn) as plainly as where it wins (fast-request tail under mixed
  load), and names the one claim that has no artifact yet.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): honest release notes, including what each
  release's failures taught.
- [apps/django_realtime/](apps/django_realtime/): the fuller demo — token
  auth, channel isolation, static files served without entering Python.
